settings.heading: Nourishing tradition
settings.text: A family kitchen, a handful of treasured recipes and a lot of desi ghee.

settings.heading: From Nani's kitchen to your table
settings.text:
Growing up in a Punjabi home, winter meant one thing: the kitchen filled with the rich aroma of whole-wheat atta slowly roasting in desi ghee. Tins of pinni were made for the whole family, shared with neighbours and packed into suitcases for relatives abroad.

When we moved to the UK, we couldn't find pinni that tasted like home – most were too sweet, made with oil, or light on dry fruits. So we started making our own, using the recipes handed down to us.

settings.heading: Slow-roasted, hand-rolled, never rushed
settings.text:
Every batch begins with pure desi ghee and flour roasted low and slow until golden and fragrant – the step that gives pinni its deep, nutty flavour. We fold in generous handfuls of almonds, cashews, melon seeds and edible gum, then roll each pinni by hand.

No palm oil, no artificial colours, no shortcuts. Just honest ingredients, made fresh in small batches and sent straight to your door.
